Unless the app adds information (e.g. via web search), it does not know about: - Recent news and publications - Brand-new tools, packages or software versions - Changes to databases, annotations or guidelines ??Examples?? # Hallucinations {background-color="#23373B" .center .middle} ## Hallucinations A **hallucination** is a fluent, confident answer that is wrong — an invented citation, gene function, function argument or statistic. ??Examples?? ## Why is it so confident? Because the model is trained to produce plausible text, a wrong answer can read exactly like a right one. Confidence in the wording is not evidence of correctness. ??Expand: training rewards plausible answers; how to check outputs?? ## Time for an exercise!
